recipes.name: Pasta Primavera with Smoked Gouda
ingredients_raw: 1 (16 ounce) package whole wheat penne pasta
1 (14.5 ounce) can stewed tomatoes, coarsely chopped

steps.text: Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Cook pasta in boiling water, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, about 11 minutes. Drain well in a colander set in the sink.

Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Stir in zucchinis, bell pepper, carrots, mushrooms, and onions; cook and stir until onions are softened and translucent, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute more. Stir in tomatoes, chicken broth, parsley, basil, oregano, and red pepper flakes.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer until sauce thickens. Stir in pasta and cook until heated through, about 2 minutes. Top with Parmesan and Gouda cheeses to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Pasta Primavera with Smoked Gouda
raw_recipe.description: This pasta with smoked Gouda cheese features whole wheat penne, zucchini, bell pepper, carrots, and Italian herbs for a savory veggie-packed dish.

review.reviewBody: This was fantastic! I used quite a bit more gouda than the recipe because I had it and a red pepper instead of green (red was curiously less expensive than the green). And of course, it took me a bit longer than 50 minutes to get it finished. Maybe I'm a slow veggie chopper. Worth the work and I will definitely make this one again!

Good recipe as written. I'm enamored w/ my own cooking sometimes...and this is one of those times. I added chicken, using a BBQ rub from World Spice...searing it then baking for awhile. Turned out flavorful and moist. I used all the called for veggies, using a yellow pepper since it's sweeter than a green one. I added some of the chicken juices and a whole can of tomato's for half a recipe. Later added some pasta water and finished the pasta off in the simmering veggies and sauce. I added way more smoked Gouda and a generous Parm/Regg. Topped it w/ Extra Sharp Cheddar Cheese and baked it at 300 degrees for 20 minutes.

I definitely deviated from the original, and consequently made it unhealthy, but it was so delicious! I added squash and zucchini, but the main difference was instead of topping with cheese, I made a sauce. I took the chicken broth and boiled it in a separate pot. I then added a slurry of 2 tbsp cornstarch and a cup and a half of milk. Once that started to thicken, I added in a cup and a half of the smoked gouda. Definitely not as healthy as the original, but I will be making this again!

I am sure this wouild just as good following directions but found this and worked with what I had. Actually made 2 pans, one for vegetarian daughter since I added bite sized chicken to ours. Was going to make hers strictly veggies but she requested the morning star "chicken" in hers. Used vegetable broth in place of chicken broth in both. Used diced tomates with basil and oregano in place of stewed tomatoes and didn't have Gouda so used shredded Fiesta blend cheese and kept on low heat covered until cheese melted and served over bow tie pasta. Enjoyed by all!

This was awesome!!! I will be making this again with some adjustments.
I'll double or triple the tomato, I'll reduce the pasta, I'll definitely add more crushed red pepper. I'm not a huge fan of oils, so I used half the evoo that was called for. I doubled all of the spices, and cooked the veggies with the garlic and spices about 10 minutes prior to adding the tomato and parsley mixture. 
Also for the look, I'll probably add some red bell pepper. So very good, amazing flavor. Just be aware, this makes A LOT of food!

Excellent recipe. I replaced the zucchini with broccoli and snap peas. I also used shredded carrots instead of sliced. I left out the stewed tomatoes and used about 1/2 cup more of the chicken broth. Delicious.
Made it gluten and dairy free and it was awesome! GF pasta and Daiya dairy free gouda

Family LOVED it!
No cheese. no chicken broth.
went lower fat with spaghetti sauce.
sprinkled Italian blend grated cheese on top of each serving.
Added cubed boneless skinless thighs for protein.

YUM!! So this was absolutely simple, easy, healthy and tasty! I was looking for a way to use up some veggies and this was perfect. The only changes I made was I used a red and orange pepper and added broccoli because that's what I had on hand. I also used veg broth since my hubby is a vegetarian. I love Gouda but didn't have any on hand so used a braid of marinated mozzarella that I diced up. Even though I made changes I don't think it changed the integrity of the dish so I still gave it 5 stars. What's nice about this dish is that you can sub different veggies or the cheese for that matter. The mozzarella I used was from Trader Joes and being that it was marinated in olive oil, red pepper flakes, and oregano it really enhanced this pasta. Will definitely be making this again. Thanks for a great recipe!

Finally tried it and LOVED it, a wonderfully tasty and healthy meal. I doubled up on the zucchini, carrots, mushrooms, tomatoes and used 1 red and 1 green bell pepper. With that it was just right for 6 servings. As a vegetarian I always try to get at least 2 - 3 servings of veggies per meal. Adjust the seasonings and cheeses accordingly. I used Italian seasoning mix and towards the end added fresh basil and oregano from my herb garden.
Thanks so much for this recipe, it's definitely on my favorites list.

Pretty tasty! Mixed votes for whether this was better or worse than homemade spaghetti. I made a few changes: omitted zucchini; 1/2 onion instead of 3; red pepper instead of green; doubled red pepper flakes & smoked gouda; added thyme & half a can of tomato paste to thicken.
I used mozzarella instead and a little more garlic and herbs.
This is an excellent recipe. The smoked gouda gives it a great flavor. I do leave out the mushrooms and use only 1 onion rather than 3.
know what you're getting into. Was not great. Didn't even want to waste the Smoked Gouda on it.
I used what vegetables I had available from my garden so onions green peppers green beans and zucchini so good! The smoked Gouda is fabulous

Loved the flavor, however, a "skillet" does not hold all of the vegetable ingredients, let alone adding the cooked pasta. This makes a lot, but is really good. The cheese adds a great dimension of flavor.
Turned out great! Substituted asparagus for mushrooms. Everybody loved it! All adults, so no children’s palettes to please, but this will be a go to from now on! Thank you!
Made as directed in recipe. Excellent dish. The finish with fresh grated cheeses is what gives the the full flavor and is a must. The more the better.
Only used 1 onion and just a sprinkle of pepper flakes because of my toddler and it was still yummy. Use a very large skillet- had to dirty two pans because didn’t realize this at first.

This was good, my 23 mo old ate it up. What helped is cuttin the zucchini & mushrooms the same size, I shredded the carrots & make them the same size as the onions. I used quinoa pasta bc I had a bunch left over that needed to be used. The only thing I did differently was omit the peppers & bc I didn’t have n e. To me, it was essentially a vegged up spaghetti sauce. Had I noticed, idda used my Italian spaghetti recipe & just added the veggies the same. Thnx.
